title: Services that run as WebAssembly
summary: A service written only in Rust, Go, C#, F#, Swift, Kotlin, Java, Dart, Ruby, Lua or C++ runs on every target. A Python service runs in web builds only (ADR 0093). A host that links the service runs it natively: Rust on macOS, Windows, Linux, iOS and Android, C# on Windows, Swift on macOS and iOS, and Kotlin on Android. The other targets run it as WebAssembly. No host links Go, F#, Java, Dart, Ruby, Lua or C++, so these services run as WebAssembly on every target. An F# service runs on the same .NET browser runtime as C# (ADR 0073). Swift uses Swift 6.3.3 and the Swift SDK for WebAssembly of the same version; set `TAC_SWIFT_WASM_SDK` to its `wasm32-unknown-wasip1` folder, and set `TAC_SWIFT_WASM_COMPILER` to the swift.org `swiftc` when Xcode's `swiftc` comes first on your `PATH` (ADR 0082). Kotlin and Dart compile to WebAssembly with garbage collection (WasmGC), and TeaVM compiles Java to WasmGC (ADR 0083); WasmGC needs Chrome or Edge 119, Firefox 120 or Safari 18.2 and newer. Dart needs the Dart SDK 3.13 or newer and has no JavaScript fallback; a build publishes `tachyon-dart.wasm` and `tachyon-dart-loader.js`. A Ruby service runs on Tachyon's mruby WebAssembly runtime, which your machine builds once with Ruby and Emscripten (ADR 0049, ADR 0054). A Lua service runs on Tachyon's Lua 5.4 WebAssembly runtime, built once with Emscripten (ADR 0085). A C++ service is a header-only `.hpp` class that Emscripten (`em++`) compiles to WebAssembly (ADR 0099). A Python service runs on Pyodide, the CPython interpreter compiled to WebAssembly. Its methods are synchronous (`async def` is refused with `TY1605`), and the manifest must select the pinned runtime with `tac.python`, as the `client/manifest.json` tab shows; without it the build fails with `TY1605` (ADR 0093). The WebAssembly service uses the same companion protocol (ADR 0035, ADR 0037, ADR 0045). Views read its fields, methods receive JSON arguments, and `Service` and `NeedsAll` are declared above its type. JavaScript and TypeScript services are not WebAssembly: the browser runs them as JavaScript, so this page has no JavaScript or TypeScript tab (see "Polyglot native services" for them).
